title: TYC 9179-1083-1 retains a 50.5-degree local orbit fit when the GALAH velocities are removed
abstract: We test velocity calibration in one published local Newtonian triple fit of TYC 9179-1083-1. We add a shared GALAH offset, add separate offsets for its two visible stars, and remove both GALAH velocities. The last two fits agree within 0.00001 solar masses. Without GALAH, masses are 0.803, 0.601 and 1.164 solar masses and mutual inclination is 50.482 degrees, against 0.779, 0.591 and 1.148 solar masses and 50.601 degrees in the source. Local mass errors grow by 36-40 percent, while the angle error grows by 5.5 percent. A free shared offset is -0.182 +/- 0.443 km/s; no offset is detected. Exact nuisance projection, derivative-step tests and IAS15 evaluation check the result. The small loss improvement is below the scale of integrator-dependent loss changes. The six remaining FEROS velocities, TESS timings and adopted shape constraints retain the local prograde solution. There are no new observations. Errors remain conditional on source weights, one shape and one local branch. Code, source hashes, fitted states and external-scratch retrieval instructions permit reproduction.

display.caption: Local fits retain similar masses and mutual inclination when GALAH offsets are free or its velocities are removed. Bars are conditional local linear errors.
